name: MIL-STD-810H Method 502.7 Procedure II low-temperature operation test at the Cold (C2) design extreme, -46 C, with at least 2 h soak after stabilization
plain_name: Prove military equipment still switches on and works after soaking at -46 C
description: Procedure II (Operation) of MIL-STD-810H Method 502.7: the test item, in its operational configuration and installed in the chamber, is brought to its low operating temperature at no more than 3 C/min, held for at least two hours after temperature stabilization, and then given an operational checkout. The operating point used here is the Cold (C2) climatic design type of Table 502.7-I, whose ambient-air cycle reaches -46 C (Canada, Alaska excluding the interior).
keywords: Prove military equipment still switches on and works after soaking at -46 C

sources.citation: MIL-STD-810H Method 502.7 Low Temperature (Department of Defense Test Method Standard, 31 January 2019)

requirements.rationale: The chamber air must be held at the C2 low extreme of -46 C (227.15 K) for the operating soak.
The machine's lowest temperature must be -46 C (227.15 K) or colder; lets machines documented by a base temperature decide.
The low temperature is held for at least two hours after the test item stabilizes (plus the stabilization time).
The item is checked out operating inside the chamber; mains- or bench-powered items need a cable port, battery items do not, so this is optional.

confirmation_note: Requirements taken from the cited procedure and independently re-verified against the source (research/v4, 2026-11-01). Users must confirm them for their own run; edits require confirmation again.
